Kr3quGh7pJA.summary: Adam Neely examines Phil Ewell's paper arguing Western music theory is framed by a white racial perspective. He covers North Indian theory, alternative frameworks, Schenker and responses to the paper.
Kr3quGh7pJA.why: HN recommends it as the canonical video on how music theory is really the theory of one Western tradition, with the raga example.

KkpqA8yG9T4.summary: MIT's Prof. Dennis Whyte explains the ARC/SPARC compact tokamak approach, in which new high-temperature superconducting magnets allow smaller and cheaper fusion reactors. He covers fusion physics, performance trends and the engineering path to net energy.
KkpqA8yG9T4.why: HN points to it as the grounded, approachable explanation of why REBCO magnets changed the outlook for fusion.

KLjgBLwH3Wc.summary: Dr. Terry Wahls tells how she used diet to manage her multiple sclerosis and get out of a wheelchair, drawing on mitochondrial biology. TED flagged the talk as health advice based on personal narrative.
KLjgBLwH3Wc.why: HN commenters point to it as a moving personal story that motivated dietary changes, though it is also cited as anecdotal evidence.

KrksBdWcZgQ.summary: Christopher Domas presents at Black Hat 2017 how page fault analysis and processor fuzzing can exhaustively search the x86 instruction set. The talk uncovers undocumented instructions and hardware bugs and shows limits of disassemblers.
KrksBdWcZgQ.why: HN recommends it as a clever, entertaining and easy-to-follow talk on finding hidden x86 instructions with the Sandsifter tool.

K4JhruinbWc.summary: A 1930s Chevrolet training film explaining the principles and development of the differential gear. It builds the idea step by step from first principles to the finished mechanism.
K4JhruinbWc.why: HN loves it as an example of old-school instructional film that makes how a differential works fully understandable in clear, simple language.

KXuZi9aeGTw.summary: Paul Turner of Google presents kernel interfaces for user-level scheduling of real threads, aiming at a uniform synchronous programming model across C++, Java, Go and Python. It introduces the switchto-style system calls behind Google's fibers.
KXuZi9aeGTw.why: HN cites it as the key explanation of cooperative, user-scheduled kernel threads and the prior art behind later async and coroutine debates.

KZjFVdU8VLI.summary: Bruce Hauman live-codes Flappy Bird in ClojureScript in about six minutes, using figwheel to hot-reload changes into the running game. The demo shows game behavior being changed interactively without restarting.
KZjFVdU8VLI.why: It is the canonical demo HN people cite for live interactive development and hot reloading, as proof the workflow is real and not smoke and mirrors.

KtQ9nt2ZeGM.summary: A long Technology Connections video arguing that public understanding of renewable energy is distorted. It covers solar economics, land use compared with ethanol corn, and battery myths such as cobalt.
KtQ9nt2ZeGM.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as an up-to-date, fact-focused case for solar and batteries that readers can cite on land use and costs.

KRcecxdGxvQ.summary: Database pioneer Michael Stonebraker argues that 'big data' is really at least four different problems: big volumes with small analytics, big analytics, velocity, and variety. He comments on where each market is heading.
KRcecxdGxvQ.why: HN points to it as a thoughtful, first-principles take from a Turing award winner that cuts through NoSQL and big data hype.

KAWA1DuvCnQ.summary: Scott Meyers' keynote at DConf 2014, drawing on 25 years of C++ experience to offer the D language community a plea about what it should avoid. It centers on the accumulated complexity and pitfalls of C++ as a cautionary tale.
KAWA1DuvCnQ.why: HN commenters bring it up whenever C++ complexity or the pitfalls of language design come up, as a witty and authoritative warning.

KTzGBJPuJwM.summary: 3Blue1Brown visualizes Feynman's lecture on the refractive index, explaining why light appears to slow down in glass and why the effect depends on color. It builds the idea from waves produced by oscillating charges in the material.
KTzGBJPuJwM.why: HN considers it among the clearest accessible explanations of what refractive index actually is and how light moves through transparent matter.

Ki_Af_o9Q9s.summary: NASA JPL engineers explain the final minutes of the Curiosity rover's entry, descent and landing on Mars, which combined aerobraking, a parachute and a skycrane. It lays out the tight sequence of events that all had to work automatically.
Ki_Af_o9Q9s.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as an awe-inspiring example of engineering problem solving and the go-to explainer on how Mars landings work.

KDRnEm-B3AI.summary: NightHawkInLight shows how to make radiative sky cooling paint from grocery and hardware store materials, including a novel calcium carbonate microsphere synthesis. The paint can cool a surface below ambient air temperature in direct sunlight without electricity.
KDRnEm-B3AI.why: It comes up whenever radiative cooling coatings are in the news, as a hands-on DIY guide that shows the approach working with household materials.

KJe9H6qS82I.summary: Tim Hutton's demonstration of SmoothLifeL, a continuous version of Conway's Game of Life using floating point values. It shows gliders traveling in any direction, rotating pairs, and elastic cord-like structures, with config details to run it yourself.
KJe9H6qS82I.why: HN points to it whenever Game of Life or cellular automata come up, as the best visual example of a mesmerizing continuous-domain alternative.

KPUlgSRn6e0.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that people in walkable, bikeable Dutch cities stay healthy because exercise is built into daily life, which he calls the gym of life. It contrasts this with car-dependent cities that require deliberate workouts.
KPUlgSRn6e0.why: HN recommends it whenever fitness, aging or cycling comes up, as the clearest statement that city design is the best public health investment.

KTHOwgpMIiU.summary: Heidi Howard's Reactive Summit 2018 talk on generalizing Paxos by weakening its original requirements. She shows Paxos is one point on a broad spectrum of consensus approaches.
KTHOwgpMIiU.why: HN recommends it as an illuminating, approachable explanation of distributed consensus.

KTJs-0EInW8.summary: Steve Yegge's Stanford seminar on GROK, Google's internal large-scale, cross-language source code analysis system. It covers how the system helps with code search and understanding across Google's huge codebase.
KTJs-0EInW8.why: HN refers to it as the main public description of Google's internal code analysis tooling, and as a precursor of ideas like LSP.

KePNhUJ2reI.summary: A PBS Space Time episode explaining how space and time swap roles inside a black hole's event horizon. It is part of the channel's black hole series.
KePNhUJ2reI.why: Recommended as the cleanest visual explanation of time and space switching roles past the horizon, and a gateway to the channel's black hole videos.

KBcxuM-qXec.summary: A minutephysics explainer showing that the Moon's path around the Sun is not a spiral but closer to a 12-sided polygon with curved corners. It argues the Moon arguably orbits the Sun rather than the Earth.
KBcxuM-qXec.why: HN links it whenever the Moon's orbit comes up, as a concise explanation of why the Moon always curves toward the Sun.

KFNxJVTJleE.summary: An Ars Technica War Stories episode in which Richard Garriott and Starr Long describe Ultima Online's planned virtual ecology and how players wrecked it. Players slaughtered the animals and also broke the in-game economy.
KFNxJVTJleE.why: HN uses it as a canonical anecdote that designers badly predicted player behavior, and in threads about UO and sharding.

KSWqx8goqSY.summary: Jason Scott of textfiles.com tells the story at DEFCON 17 of being sued for two billion dollars by a scammer who plagued him and others for over a decade. The talk is tragic and funny, covering what he learned about misleading schemes.
KSWqx8goqSY.why: HN commenters recommend it as a great, hilarious talk about legal threats and cease and desist letters.

K_q-xnYRugQ.summary: Technology Connections explains weaknesses in the US electrical system, centering on how cord and circuit ratings can mismatch and cause fires. It covers extension cords, power strips and plug history in about 25 minutes.
K_q-xnYRugQ.why: HN points to it as a clear explanation of why under-rated extension cords and daisy-chained power strips are dangerous.

KaOC9danxNo.summary: Commander Chris Hadfield performs a revised version of David Bowie's Space Oddity, recorded aboard the International Space Station. It was released as a music video in 2013.
KaOC9danxNo.why: Commenters recommend it for the sense of wonder and chills it gives, and bring it up in threads about Bowie, space and astronauts.

KqFNbCcyFkk.summary: Super Eyepatch Wolf analyzes why The Simpsons declined after its golden age, pointing to changes in the writers' room and a shift in the style and complexity of its comedy.
KqFNbCcyFkk.why: HN treats it as the definitive explanation of the Simpsons decline, recommended in every thread asking when the golden age ended.

K3lP3BhvnSo.summary: Ben Felix explains how central bank money creation and quantitative easing actually work, and what they do and do not imply for asset prices and currency. He addresses the common belief that the Fed prints unlimited money and props up markets.
K3lP3BhvnSo.why: HN users point to it to correct the 'money printer go brrr' view and as a clear explanation of how banks create money through loans.

KbB0FjPg0mw.summary: Lecture 1 of Harvard's Statistics 110 with Joe Blitzstein, introducing sample spaces, the naive definition of probability, counting, binomial coefficients and the sampling table.
KbB0FjPg0mw.why: Recommended on Ask HN threads as a high-quality free probability course for relearning math or building an ML foundation.

KgzQuE1pR1w.summary: A short clip from Bill Hicks' final special, Revelations, in which he describes life as just a ride. It is a philosophical, calming monologue.
KgzQuE1pR1w.why: Offered as a pick-me-up and calming perspective when people feel lost or stressed.

Kxryv2XrnqM.summary: Tony Seba's 2016 keynote argues that batteries, electric vehicles, self-driving cars and solar will converge to disrupt energy and transportation. He predicts by 2030 all new vehicles will be electric and autonomous and that oil and other fossil fuels will be obsolete.
Kxryv2XrnqM.why: Cited as a well-argued case that solar plus batteries and EVs will reach a tipping point sooner than mainstream forecasts expect.

KDpNQQqdSh8.summary: Part 1 of an episode of the British educational TV series The Secret Life of Machines, about how vacuum cleaners work and their history. It mixes humor with explanation of household technology.
KDpNQQqdSh8.why: HN recommends the series as an entertaining way to learn how everyday machines work, enough to start debugging them.

KEoGrbKAyKE.summary: Who Killed Captain Alex is Uganda's first action movie, made for under $200 by Nabwana IGG in Wakaliga. This version has English subtitles and a video joker (VJ Emmie) providing running commentary.
KEoGrbKAyKE.why: HN recommends it as a fun, surprisingly entertaining low-budget film made better by the live-style commentary.

KINIAgRpkDA.summary: Rob Pike's GopherCon 2016 talk on the design of the Go assembler, explaining why Go uses a common assembly language translated to each architecture.
KINIAgRpkDA.why: HN points to it for background on how the Go toolchain targets many architectures and why its assembler is designed that way.

KJPdbp1An2s.summary: A long live-coded DJ set in which Sam Aaron creates all the music in real time by writing code in his Sonic Pi system. It demonstrates algorithmic electronic music performance.
KJPdbp1An2s.why: HN people recommend it as the most impressive demonstration of live coding music, especially to those curious about programmable music.

KNWh6Kw3ejQ.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything segment on the real facts of the McDonald's hot coffee lawsuit, covering the severity of the burns and the corporate PR campaign that painted it as frivolous.
KNWh6Kw3ejQ.why: HN cites it as a quick, entertaining explainer to correct the myth of the frivolous coffee lawsuit.

K_nnUbX7uuQ.summary: A documentary on how Cornwall became a hub for the world's communications, from the first transatlantic radio signal to modern undersea fibre cables. It describes how cable landing stations and the systems are put together.
K_nnUbX7uuQ.why: Recommended as a rare look at the unmarked buildings and infrastructure where undersea cables come ashore.

K_oET45GzMI.summary: A 1997 BBC documentary on Black Wednesday in 1992, when sterling was forced out of the Exchange Rate Mechanism. It covers the crisis from the British government side, including George Soros's trade and political mistakes.
K_oET45GzMI.why: HN recommends it as a detailed documentary on the Soros-versus-Bank-of-England episode.

KdnGPQaICjk.summary: The opening episode of Ted Nelson's Computers for Cynics series, in which he casts doubt on conventional accounts of computer basics. He argues that conventions and packaging are mistaken for technology.
KdnGPQaICjk.why: HN likes it for Nelson's habit of reframing computing history so that past decisions look arbitrary.

KeLBd2EJLOU.summary: Part two of Herb Sutter's C++ and Beyond 2012 session on atomic weapons, a deep dive into the C++ memory model, atomics, memory ordering, and hardware behavior. It ends with the modern meaning of volatile.
KeLBd2EJLOU.why: HN recommends it as an in-depth, practical introduction to atomics and weak versus strong memory ordering, relevant to ARM and Rust as well as C++.

KTjnt_WSJu8.summary: A capture of Second Reality, the real-time audiovisual demo by Future Crew first shown at Assembly 1993, recorded from a 486DX2-66 with a Gravis Ultrasound. It showcases the peak of early 1990s PC demoscene techniques.
KTjnt_WSJu8.why: HN points to it as one of the best and most formative early PC demos, a touchstone of demoscene history.

KVl5kMXz1vA.summary: Philosopher Jeffrey Kaplan summarizes Peter Singer's 1972 essay 'Famine, Affluence, and Morality', arguing that failing to give to save lives is morally comparable to letting a child drown. It is a short lecture on the argument's structure.
KVl5kMXz1vA.why: HN recommends it as the best short exposition of Singer's argument for a duty to give.

K1xnYFCZ9Yg.summary: Stated Clearly explains the RNA world hypothesis, which resolves the chicken-or-egg problem of genes versus enzymes by proposing that RNA once did both jobs. It outlines how evolution could begin with RNA chains alone.
K1xnYFCZ9Yg.why: HN recommends it as an engaging, brief overview of the RNA world idea.

KUdHIatS36A.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on the Ferguson shooting, racial inequality in policing, and the militarization of local police forces in the US.
KUdHIatS36A.why: HN cites it as a well-made explainer on police militarization that remains relevant years later.

KVN_0qvuhhw.summary: Tim Minchin performs Prejudice, a comedic song about the power of words and the language used to abuse and demean.
KVN_0qvuhhw.why: HN cites it in arguments about the force of words, including the long debates over the GIMP name and username filtering.

KcfFJ6pNEZk.summary: A timelapse of Notch (Markus Persson) creating his Ludum Dare 21 entry, Prelude of the Chambered, from scratch in 48 hours.
KcfFJ6pNEZk.why: HN recommends it as a way to demystify game creation and shows what an experienced developer can build in a 48-hour jam.

KdfHVcU8U7U.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science demonstrates an X-ray fluorescence gun that measures chemical composition, tears it down, analyzes its failure, and discusses a new XRF technology appearing on eBay.
KdfHVcU8U7U.why: HN recommends it as a hands-on introduction to XRF and a fascinating teardown showing the x-ray tube and beryllium windows.

KkMDCCdjyW8.summary: First lecture of Stanford's CS106A Programming Methodology by Mehran Sahami, giving a course overview and starting on programming. The course teaches software engineering principles using Java.
KkMDCCdjyW8.why: HN suggests it as a free lecture for beginners that eases them into writing readable, reusable code.

Klkpk_hO4FQ.summary: Defense analyst H I Sutton argues that a new type of Chinese landing barge can only be explained by planning for an amphibious assault, in particular on Taiwan.
Klkpk_hO4FQ.why: HN points to it as the best source on why these barges are designed for invasion and how they overcome limited landing beaches.

Ks-_Mh1QhMc.summary: Amy Cuddy's TED talk arguing that adopting expansive postures, or power posing, can boost feelings of confidence and affect success. A note on the video points to the later reproducibility debate over its findings.
Ks-_Mh1QhMc.why: HN brings it up in threads about impostor syndrome, confidence, and body language as an interesting talk on faking it until you feel it.

Ks0SOn8hjG8.summary: Computerphile interview with Prof. Ross Anderson on how Chip and PIN payment systems are being compromised, and the attacks researchers have seen.
Ks0SOn8hjG8.why: HN points to it as a good overview of Chip and PIN attacks and the consumer-liability downsides.

Kvsvd67XUKw.summary: Dennis Gustafsson, creator of Teardown, presents how he parallelized the physics solver for an upcoming game, followed by a Q&A. The talk was given at the Better Software Conference 2025.
Kvsvd67XUKw.why: HN points to it as a practical example of solving a tricky multithreading problem, including using a spinlock to speed up a real-time physics solver.

KxGRhd_iWuE.summary: A short English-subtitled clip of Shuzo Matsuoka, a retired Japanese tennis player turned motivational speaker, delivering a never-give-up pep talk. It is a well-known Japanese internet meme.
KxGRhd_iWuE.why: HN commenters post it as a quick dose of encouragement, or as a joke reply.

K8gV05nS7mc.summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking whether time began at the Big Bang. It explains that the Big Bang is not what most people were taught and what 'start' of the universe really means.
K8gV05nS7mc.why: Used as a go-to reference for cosmology questions about the beginning of time and the universe's scale.

KT18KJouHWg.summary: Veritasium explains how investigators caught the Golden State Killer using forensic genealogy, matching crime scene DNA to distant relatives in public genealogy databases. It also covers the privacy implications of DNA databases.
KT18KJouHWg.why: HN points to it as the go-to explanation of how police can identify anyone through relatives' DNA tests, in privacy and genetics threads.

KZazEM8cgt0.summary: A short Frank Zappa interview clip on the decline of the music business, contrasting old cigar-chomping executives with younger industry people.
KZazEM8cgt0.why: HN quotes it as a prescient take on industry decline and on how young, hip managers can be more conservative than the old guard.

Kas0tIxDvrg.summary: A short 3Blue1Brown primer on exponential and logistic growth, using early COVID-19 case data to show how epidemics grow and eventually level off. It explains why small changes in growth rate make enormous differences in outcomes.
Kas0tIxDvrg.why: During the early COVID-19 period, HN commenters linked it as the clearest quick explanation of what exponential growth means for an epidemic.

KbgvSi35n6o.summary: Captain Disillusion debunks the Cicret Bracelet, a crowdfunded wearable that claimed to project a touchscreen onto the wrist. He looks at the concept, design, execution and fundraising.
KbgvSi35n6o.why: HN uses the Cicret Bracelet as shorthand for vaporware, applied to products like the Humane AI Pin, and praises Captain Disillusion's production values.

K1WrHH-WtaA.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs explaining how sales and marketing people take over mature companies from product people, leading to product decline.
K1WrHH-WtaA.why: HN cites it whenever a company stagnates, from Intel to Boeing, to explain what happens when salespeople or finance run the business.

K8kua5B5K3I.summary: Motherboard's 2014 visit to a secretive Bitcoin mining operation in a repurposed factory in Liaoning, China, one of six sites producing about 4,050 bitcoins a month. It shows the machines and the workers' living conditions.
K8kua5B5K3I.why: HN links it as a rare look inside a large Chinese mining operation, with its deafening machine noise and workers' conditions.

KAm7qAKAXwI.summary: Applied Science explains how retail anti-theft tags work. A tiny magnetostrictive strip acts as a mechanical oscillator excited by a magnetic field, and magnetizing or demagnetizing it arms or disarms the tag.
KAm7qAKAXwI.why: HN recommends it as an informative explanation of what those tags are, especially in threads about implants and RFID.

KBMU6l6GsdM.summary: Short US Missile Defense Agency footage of the December 2008 free-flight hover test of Lockheed Martin's Multiple Kill Vehicle. The test showed it hovering for 20 seconds while tracking a simulated target.
KBMU6l6GsdM.why: HN cites it as striking evidence of long-standing kinetic interceptor and hover-control technology.

KCkbp4wurW0.summary: Gameplay footage of the original 1986 Macintosh version of Dark Castle by Silicon Beach Software. The uploader argues the original is a great game that was tarnished by inferior ports.
KCkbp4wurW0.why: HN uses it to show a classic early Mac game, noting its low-latency input and early audio showcase.

KClAPipnKqw.summary: Tanya Reilly's LeadDev talk on glue work, the invisible coordination and support tasks engineers do that keep teams successful but can hurt careers.
KClAPipnKqw.why: HN refers to it in career and promotion discussions, including its warning about doing glue work too early in your career.

KRvv0QdruMQ.summary: Kurzgesagt asks whether advanced civilizations could have existed on Earth in the deep past and left little evidence. It looks at time as a dimension for searching for alien civilizations and the limits of the geological record.
KRvv0QdruMQ.why: HN brings it up in threads on ancient civilizations and detecting past technology in geology.

KX_0c9R4Fng.summary: A DEF CON 23 talk by Marc Rogers and Kevin Mahaffey walking through the architecture of the Tesla Model S, what Tesla got right and wrong, and how the interconnected systems can be hacked. It also covers the data the car collects.
KX_0c9R4Fng.why: HN cites it as a detailed technical reference on Tesla's security design, especially the firewalling of infotainment from the CAN bus.

KZeIEiBrT_w.summary: A Veritasium video on how a feud between Russian mathematicians led to Markov chains and the modern prediction algorithms built on them. It covers the history and the math behind them.
KZeIEiBrT_w.why: HN recommends it as an excellent, detailed history of Markov chains, often in threads on Markov models and language models.

KZokQov_aH0.summary: Joseph Anderson's long critique of Jonathan Blow's puzzle game The Witness, covering its gameplay, its hundreds of puzzles and its philosophical pretensions. He argues it is a great game that he nonetheless advises against playing.
KZokQov_aH0.why: HN uses it mainly as a critical review of the game, saying it captures a lack of respect for the player, though one commenter suggests watching it after finishing.

KfqtYfaILHw.summary: Deviant Ollam's DEF CON 17 talk explains how legally checking a firearm in luggage can be the most secure way to fly with valuable tech. It covers firearm transport rules and luggage locks.
KfqtYfaILHw.why: HN cites it as a famous talk on luggage security whenever TSA keys or baggage theft come up.

KkMP328eU5Q.summary: The first part of Extra History's series on the Bronze Age Collapse, introducing the Egyptians, Hittites, Assyrians, and Mycenaeans and their interlinked system of trade, agriculture, and war before the Sea Peoples arrive.
KkMP328eU5Q.why: HN points to it as an entertaining, approachable docu-series on how interconnected civilizations can collapse, often in discussions of societal fragility.

Ko4V3G4NqII.summary: An edited excerpt of Steve Jobs introducing Mac OS X at Macworld San Francisco in 2000. It covers the Aqua interface, Quartz graphics built on PDF, and the Classic, Carbon and Cocoa application environments.
Ko4V3G4NqII.why: HN commenters cite it as primary-source evidence of what Jobs actually said about Mac OS X's design, open-source kernel and NeXT-based transition.

Kp7FkLBRpKg.summary: A short clip from the Dutch program Nieuwsuur in which Julian Assange appears to suggest that murdered DNC staffer Seth Rich was the source of the WikiLeaks DNC emails.
Kp7FkLBRpKg.why: HN links it as the primary source for Assange's remarks hinting at Seth Rich as the leak source.

KsLi7HgSuhI.summary: Onboard footage of Timo Bernhard setting the Nurburgring Nordschleife lap record of 5:19.546 in the Porsche 919 Hybrid Evo, beating Stefan Bellof's 35-year-old time. The car reaches 369 km/h.
KsLi7HgSuhI.why: HN uses it to show what a skilled human driver can do in a car, for example in self-driving and motorsport threads.

KtHQGs3zFAM.summary: Jim Coplien and Bob Martin debate test-driven development and unit testing in an InfoQ video that grew out of a JAOO 2007 dispute. They also touch on design and architecture.
KtHQGs3zFAM.why: HN points to it as a fun, substantive exchange between two experienced practitioners on TDD's value.

KtYkyB35zkk.summary: Tim Minchin performs his comedic beat poem 'Storm', a roughly nine-minute rant against homeopathy, alternative medicine and woolly thinking. It is delivered as a fast, rhyming monologue built around an encounter at a dinner party.
KtYkyB35zkk.why: HN commenters link it as a funny, quotable takedown of alternative medicine and cite its lines (such as 'alternative medicine that works is called medicine') in threads on homeopathy.

KuG_CeEZV6w.summary: The Hydraulic Press Channel folds an A3 sheet of paper past the supposed seven-fold limit and then crushes it with a press. It is a short, quirky experiment.
KuG_CeEZV6w.why: Linked in paper folding threads as a fun demonstration and as the video that made the channel famous.

Kzpv47o80eg.summary: Rachel and Jun film Toyota Home Aichi installing a prefabricated house unit in Japan, with the assembly and roof waterproofing completed in about half a day.
Kzpv47o80eg.why: Cited in prefab and housing threads as proof that high-quality modular homes can be assembled on site in hours.

K0Tsa3smr1w.summary: Shaun Lebron surveys 50 years of Lisp editing history and forgotten innovations in structural editing. He argues future Clojure editors could learn from them, and covers ideas like Parinfer.
K0Tsa3smr1w.why: HN cites it as a summary of known attempts at structural and Lisp editors.

K2WhU77ihw8.summary: Hugh Jeffreys tests the iPhone 14 Pro and finds that swapping genuine parts between phones disables features, concluding that third-party repair is not really viable despite Apple's Self Service Repair program.
K2WhU77ihw8.why: HN cites it as evidence of Apple's parts pairing and in right-to-repair discussions.

K3meJyiYWFw.summary: A Google I/O 2014 fireside chat in which members of the Android platform team answer questions about why the platform works the way it does. It is moderated by developer advocate Reto Meier.
K3meJyiYWFw.why: HN cites specific moments, such as the team's stance that Java is the official language and its answers on Scala and permission-revoking.

K6geOms33Dk.summary: Peter Sripol builds and flies an RC aeroplane whose wings are rotating KFC buckets, using the Magnus effect (Flettner rotors) for lift. It is a hobbyist experiment in unconventional aerodynamics.
K6geOms33Dk.why: HN cites it as a fun, concrete demonstration that Magnus-effect rotating cylinders can generate enough lift to fly.

KEDrMriKsFM.summary: Promotional video from Zapata Racing showing Franky Zapata flying the Flyboard Air prototype, claiming autonomous flight to 10,000 feet, 150 km/h top speed and 10 minutes of endurance.
KEDrMriKsFM.why: Cited in threads on personal flight and hoverboards as evidence that jet-powered personal flight devices really exist.

KEkrWRHCDQU.summary: A comedic Kung Fury spinoff in which Hackerman demonstrates 'hacking' household objects through time. It parodies 1980s hacker tropes.
KEkrWRHCDQU.why: Posted as a joke whenever HN threads touch on hacking or hackers.

KHJbSvidohg.summary: A 20-second clip from the Mel Brooks comedy Blazing Saddles featuring the line about morons.
KHJbSvidohg.why: Used as a joke reply to express exasperation at foolish behavior in HN threads.

KM6X2MEl7R8.summary: Adam Neely explains that Warner Music claimed his video, which defended their copyright in a lawsuit, over a work whose copyright they had lost. He calls it an ironic and absurd claim, and the claim was later released.
KM6X2MEl7R8.why: HN cites it as a prime example of the absurdity of YouTube's automated copyright claim system.

KMU0tzLwhbE.summary: A short clip of Steve Ballmer's famous sweaty chant of the word Developers, repeated over and over.
KMU0tzLwhbE.why: HN uses it purely as a joke, quoting the chant when threads discuss how much a company or platform depends on developers.

KN0K58EfJSg.summary: A short clip from Microsoft's 1995 Judgement Day event in which Bill Gates is inserted into Doom as a promo for Windows 95 and DirectX gaming. It was never publicly released at the time.
KN0K58EfJSg.why: Cited mostly as a retro-tech curiosity about Microsoft's push into PC gaming, and sometimes as a joke.

KNqozQ8uaV8.summary: A one-minute AJ+ clip of a Palestinian woman confronting an Israeli settler in Sheikh Jarrah over taking her family's home.
KNqozQ8uaV8.why: Cited critically in threads on Israel and Palestine as an example of settler takeovers.

KO8L9tKR4CY.summary: Short footage from a NASA space suit test in which a technician is exposed to near-vacuum after an accidental depressurization. It shows the instantaneous effects on a human body.
KO8L9tKR4CY.why: Cited as real footage of someone surviving brief vacuum exposure.

KOHQQyAKY14.summary: Jim Keller, CTO of Tenstorrent, talks at Samsung Foundry's SAFE 2021 about building AI silicon through modular, provable design. The talk also touches on Tenstorrent's RISC-V Ascalon core.
KOHQQyAKY14.why: HN cites it as a source on Tenstorrent's wide-issue RISC-V Ascalon CPU in RISC-V threads.

KP_bKvXkoC4.summary: Gleb Smirnoff explains why Netflix built its own CDN on FreeBSD and NGINX, and how Netflix and NGINX Inc. collaborate on the software. It is a conference talk about open-source choices for video delivery.
KP_bKvXkoC4.why: Cited in FreeBSD vs Linux debates as the source for why Netflix chose FreeBSD, with commenters reading the GPL as the main factor.

KRBIH0CA7ZU.summary: An internal 1991 NeXT video in which Steve Jobs explains the company's product and marketing strategy. It shows NeXT aiming at the Unix workstation market.
KRBIH0CA7ZU.why: HN cites it as primary-source evidence that NeXT adopted Unix as a means to reach the workstation market rather than out of ideology.

KSg3fU9XWow.summary: A short compilation of Steve Jobs giving his opinions on Microsoft, including calling it opportunistic and lacking taste. It also touches on the role of big tech companies in showing what is possible.
KSg3fU9XWow.why: Cited in discussions of Microsoft's standing and culture as Jobs' blunt critique.

KSjrYWPxsG8.summary: Chess YouTuber agadmator reports that YouTube took down his podcast with Hikaru Nakamura as harmful or dangerous content. It was later restored.
KSjrYWPxsG8.why: Cited as an example of automated content moderation misfiring, notably the incident where chess talk was flagged as hate speech.

KWbLOFGSEDo.summary: A short 2010 clip of someone playing the Xbox 360 Kinect Joy Ride racing game, with picture-in-picture footage of the player. The uploader jokes about whether the game has auto-steering.
KWbLOFGSEDo.why: It is cited only as a joke or passing reference in Kinect and driving threads, not as something to watch.

KYbM-3E11Qo.summary: Boeing rehearses its 2015 Paris Air Show flying display of the Vietnam Airlines 787-9 Dreamliner, including a very steep takeoff and tight turns.
KYbM-3E11Qo.why: Posted as supporting footage when threads discuss spectacular airliner demos and steep takeoffs.

KjB6r-HDDI0.summary: A Wayne's World (1992) movie clip in which Wayne and Garth tell Benjamin they will not bow to any sponsor, that they are not in it for the money.
KjB6r-HDDI0.why: It is posted purely as a joke in threads about sponsorship, ads and selling out.

Km5XQxRrQvw.summary: A short Silicon Valley clip in which Jian Yang copies popular apps and launches a new Pied Piper, and Seppen listens.
Km5XQxRrQvw.why: Used as a joke in threads about app clones and the TikTok ban.

KnIAAkSNtqo.summary: Jordan Peterson's testimony at the Canadian Senate hearing on Bill C16, which added gender identity and expression to protected grounds. He argues against compelled speech.
KnIAAkSNtqo.why: Referenced as the hearing that propelled Peterson to public visibility and as a source on the compelled speech debate.

KodqIPMbyUg.summary: A 1988 Saturday Night Live fake commercial for a bank that keeps your pocket change and claims to make money on volume.
KodqIPMbyUg.why: HN uses it as a joke reference whenever a business loses money per transaction and says it will make it up in volume.

KpPE85Jogjw.summary: A short clip from Ready Player One in which Nolan Sorrento pitches selling ad space in the Oasis, including a joke about selling much of a user's visual field.
KpPE85Jogjw.why: HN posts it as a joke whenever a company pushes intrusive advertising or metaverse monetization.

Kr7AONv3FSg.summary: A one-minute trimmed clip from The Dark Knight showing the cell phone sonar surveillance system.
Kr7AONv3FSg.why: Used purely as a joke or meme when threads touch on tracking and surveillance.

KrbWbBYAolo.summary: FOSDEM 2020 talk from Collabora on pressure-vessel, an experimental mechanism that puts Steam games in containers on Linux. It covers using namespaces to give games their own runtime library stack independent of the host.
KrbWbBYAolo.why: HN references it as the explanation of how Valve uses containers for Linux game compatibility.

Kua9cY8q_EI.summary: Linus Tech Tips replicates the Threadripper workstation Linus Torvalds built for himself, discussing the parts such as the CPU and cooler.
Kua9cY8q_EI.why: HN references it when people ask about dev machines and to show how large the CPU and cooler are.

Kv9JYqhFV-M.summary: A short clip of a 2014 Mercedes S-Class driving itself with adaptive cruise control and Active Lane Assist, with the hands-on-wheel timeout defeated.
Kv9JYqhFV-M.why: Used in driver-assistance threads as an example of defeating hands-on-wheel checks on level 2 systems.

KvMxLpce3Xw.summary: A short clip from Star Trek (2009) showing young Spock learning at a Vulcan school with an immersive, machine-driven teaching system.
KvMxLpce3Xw.why: Cited as a pop-culture image of programming humans or AI tutoring in threads on education, VR and AI.

KwU56Rv0OXM.summary: A lecture by Noam Chomsky on thought control in democratic societies, covering propaganda and manufacturing consent. The upload has no description.
KwU56Rv0OXM.why: Mostly appears in lists of links on manufacturing consent rather than with individual recommendations.

KyLqUf4cdwc.summary: A 2007 video of someone trying to write Perl code using Windows Vista's speech recognition, with hilariously bad results.
KyLqUf4cdwc.why: Used as a running joke in discussions of programming by voice.
